items.title: Nepal in talks with China to reopen Tatopani border point: Minister Lamsal
items.summary: Kathmandu, October 6 Minister for Infrastructure Development Sunil Lamsal said the government is in continuous dialogue with China to reopen the Tatopani border point. Lamsal made the statement at a meeting of the Parliamentary Special Committee on the Impact of Climate Change in the Himalayas, Climate Justice and the Bhotekoshi-Trishuli Disaster held at Singha Durbar. items.title: Nepal’s growth to slow to 3.7 percent after devastating Rasuwa flood
items.summary: The World Bank estimates $1.66 billion in direct damage to physical assets, with infrastructure accounting for 83 percent of the losses.

items.title: Nepal’s disaster panel is debating what to call the Bhotekoshi floods. ‘Himalayan tsunami’ isn’t on the list
items.summary: Prime Minister Balendra Shah used the term at the UN, but experts on the government panel say they are considering other names for the August 26 disaster.

items.title: Nepal scales back flood search as Rs559b reconstruction effort begins
items.summary: The government has suspended search and rescue operations for Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods except in emergencies, directing authorities to accelerate reconstruction and rehabilitation in flood-hit areas.
